title: Urine culture status before elective urological instrumentation
logic: If an elective procedure instrumenting the urinary tract (prostatectomy, cystolithotomy, urethrotomy, TURBT, stent change) is booked without a recorded urine culture result or a documented treated-bacteriuria course, the booking is incomplete — instrumenting infected urine seeds sepsis.
action: Flag the booking; prompt urine culture and, if positive, a completed treatment course before listing; emergencies bypass with culture taken at catheterisation and treatment running.

title: Pain-onset time is a required field for acute scrotum
logic: If an acute scrotal presentation is being recorded, time of pain onset must be captured — it drives the torsion salvage window and every downstream decision.
action: Make pain-onset time mandatory on the acute scrotum form; auto-display elapsed time on the referral and theatre booking.

title: Acute scrotum is torsion until proven otherwise
logic: If a male (particularly adolescent) presents with acute scrotal pain, torsion is the working diagnosis; imaging or observation must not delay surgical exploration when clinical suspicion exists, and the salvage window is measured in hours from pain onset.
action: Raise an emergency alert with the elapsed-time-from-onset displayed; route directly to surgical review and emergency theatre listing; block pathways that schedule ultrasound as a prerequisite when a capable theatre is available.

title: Obstructed infected kidney requires decompression in hours
logic: If imaging or strong clinical evidence shows an obstructing ureteric stone or hydronephrosis together with fever, rigors, or sepsis markers, the patient has an obstructed infected kidney — antibiotics alone cannot sterilise it.
action: Trigger the emergency pathway: sepsis bundle plus urgent decompression decision (JJ stent or nephrostomy, whichever the facility delivers fastest); if neither exists on site, initiate emergency transfer rather than admit-and-observe.

title: Blocked irrigation catheter after prostate or bladder surgery
logic: If a patient on continuous bladder irrigation after prostatectomy or bladder surgery develops absent outflow, suprapubic pain, or a palpably distending bladder, clot retention is presumed — a blocked catheter under irrigation is an emergency, not a routine nursing task.
action: Alert for immediate bedside action: stop irrigation inflow, bladder washout to evacuate clot, and urgent surgical review if washout fails; escalate to theatre for clot evacuation and haemostasis where bleeding continues.

title: Visible haematuria classifies to the urothelial cancer pathway
logic: If visible painless haematuria is recorded in an adult (especially over 40, a smoker, or with schistosomiasis exposure), classify to the haematuria work-up pathway: cystoscopy plus upper tract imaging; a bladder mass found classifies to EXPEDITED TURBT at central hospital.
action: Auto-open the haematuria pathway with cystoscopy and imaging orders proposed; flag any visible-haematuria episode older than 6 weeks without a recorded cystoscopy plan; treat bilharzia where ova confirmed without closing the cancer question.

title: Urological prophylaxis targets urinary flora and follows culture
logic: If a urological procedure is booked, prophylaxis is a single intravenous dose at induction targeting gram-negative urinary flora — gentamicin, or cefazolin, or both per local policy and renal function — and is directed by the urine culture result where one exists; established urosepsis converts to a treatment course.
action: Prompt agent selection at induction showing the latest urine culture and renal function; record administration time; suppress prophylaxis prompts when a treatment course is charted.

title: Post-prostatectomy irrigation and haemoglobin surveillance
logic: If a patient is on continuous bladder irrigation after prostatectomy, effluent colour and catheter patency are charted at least hourly for the first 12 hours, with haemoglobin checked per protocol; darkening effluent, haemodynamic change, or falling haemoglobin escalates to surgical review; after transurethral resection, confusion or vomiting raises TUR (dilutional hyponatraemia) syndrome and mandates urgent sodium measurement.
action: Generate hourly irrigation observations for 12 hours then per protocol; alert on darkening effluent, obstruction, haemodynamic triggers, or neurological change; propose sodium check on any post-TUR neurological symptom.

title: Bladder tumour surveillance after TURBT
logic: If TURBT histology confirms bladder cancer, non-muscle-invasive disease requires check cystoscopy at 3 months and a risk-stratified ongoing cystoscopic surveillance schedule; muscle-invasive disease routes to MDT for radical treatment decision instead of surveillance.
action: At histology sign-off, auto-book the 3-month check cystoscopy for non-muscle-invasive disease and generate the surveillance schedule; route muscle-invasive results to MDT within 2 weeks; flag any confirmed tumour with no follow-up event booked.

title: Trial of void and flow review close the retention episode
logic: If a catheter was placed for retention or removed after prostate/urethral surgery, a documented trial of void outcome is required; failed trials route back to the surgical pathway, and successful ones get a flow and symptom review at 4–6 weeks — an episode is not closed by catheter removal alone.
action: Auto-generate the trial-of-void task at catheter removal with outcome capture; book the 4–6 week review on success; re-open the surgical worklist entry on failure.
